h2: Plumber Seminyak – Villa Repairs Between Check-Ins
intro: When a mixer drips at 7 am before the next guest arrives, you need a plumber Seminyak villa managers actually call — someone who shows up, traces the fault, and fixes it properly. I work solo across Petitenget, Oberoi and Basangkasa, handling taps, toilets, pumps, hot water and pool equipment in villas that have been running for 15–25 years. No dispatch queue, no hand-off: one person from diagnosis to finished job.

sections.h3: Why Seminyak Villas Break Down Faster Than You'd Expect
sections.text: Dense plots with shared walls mean a slow leak behind a bathroom partition can soak a neighbour's ceiling before anyone notices. Older pipework in many local villas corrodes internally, so pressure drops and mixers seize without visible damage outside. High-occupancy rentals push septic tanks past capacity during rainy season, and flooded lanes back-pressure into drains. I come on site, isolate the source, and repair or replace the part — whether that's a cistern valve, a pump seal, or a full basin re-fit between check-ins.

sections.h3: What to Send Me on WhatsApp Before I Arrive
sections.text: A short video of the problem (running tap, dripping cistern, low-flow shower) plus a photo of the affected fixture saves a second visit. If it's a pressure issue, tell me which taps are weak and whether the pool pump is cycling constantly. For hidden leaks, note where you first spotted dampness and roughly how long ago. I'll reply with what I need to bring and an estimate based on what you've shown — no obligation until we agree on the scope.

sections.h3: Small Habits That Save Seminyak Villas from Big Bills
sections.text: Flush a bucket of water through each toilet weekly so mineral build-up doesn't lock the flapper shut. In Petitenget and Oberoi lanes, clear leaf debris from surface drains before the wet season peaks, because once water overtops a septic inlet there's no easy reset. Swap mixer cartridges every six months; a worn seal costs minutes to replace but weeks of damage if ignored. Keep the pump room ventilated too — trapped humidity accelerates corrosion on older hot-water tanks.

sections.h3: Working in Tight Plots Across Basangkasa & Neighbouring Lanes
sections.text: Small footprints and shared party walls mean I often work in crawl-space conditions under basins or behind garden walls to reach a pipe joint. Compact tools for exactly this: narrow wrenches, flexible hoses, and portable leak detectors that fit where a full crew can't. If your villa sits between two rentals with no rear access, send me a photo of the layout on WhatsApp and I'll plan the approach before arriving.

faq.q: Do you handle both plumbing and pool-related pipework in one visit?
faq.a: Yes — taps, toilets, pumps, hot-water systems and pool circulation lines all fall under one call-out. If the fault turns out to be purely electrical or structural, I'll tell you straight and point you in the right direction.

faq.q: Can you fix things during a guest stay without disrupting them?
faq.a: In most cases yes; I schedule around the villa's occupancy and keep noise and mess to a minimum. Send a quick photo on WhatsApp first and I'll confirm whether it's a 20-minute swap or needs a longer window.

faq.q: What if the leak source isn't obvious from the surface?
faq.a: I bring portable detection gear for tracing hidden pipes behind walls or under slabs. You don't need to guess where the fault is — just describe what you see (damp patch, pressure loss, unusual smell) and I'll locate it on site.
